title: T1001.001 — Data Obfuscation - Junk Data
subtitle: Watch padding break hash-based defenses in eight steps, and watch analytics catch what the hashes miss.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: First beacon with a fixed size
steps.caption: The implant sends its first check-in: a POST with a body of exactly 128 bytes, repeated every 60 seconds.
steps.defender: record the baseline size and cadence per host - you will compare against it later.

fields.detail: The implant sends its first check-in: a POST with a body of exactly 128 bytes, repeated every 60 sec

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Implant starts adding junk data
steps.caption: The attacker enables the padding option, and the implant appends 0 to 900 random bytes to each beacon.
steps.defender: padding is built at runtime on the victim, so no two beacons share content or a hash.

fields.detail: The attacker enables the padding option, and the implant appends 0 to 900 random bytes to each beaco

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Beacon sizes become random
steps.caption: The proxy now sees bodies of 713, 244, 988, then 61 bytes.
steps.defender: content signatures stop matching, but the steady one-minute cadence and the same URI remain.

steps.title: Screenshot upload with junk appended
steps.caption: The implant captures a screenshot, appends junk, and uploads it to a cloud note service.
steps.defender: the file name and URI template stay constant while the hash changes on every upload.

steps.title: Hash-based detection misses
steps.caption: Antivirus and file-reputation checks compare the upload hash to known-bad lists and return clean, because the hash is new every time.
steps.defender: flow records still show who talked to what, and how many bytes moved.

steps.title: Size-variance analytics fire
steps.caption: An analytics rule compares the beacon size spread against the host baseline: standard deviation 310 bytes versus a normal 12.
steps.defender: wide spread plus steady cadence is a strong C2 signal that padding cannot hide.

fields.detail: An analytics rule compares the beacon size spread against the host baseline: standard deviation 310

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Analyst hunts for the URI template
steps.caption: The analyst searches proxy logs for the same URI pattern and finds it on four hosts, one of them newly infected.
steps.defender: the template is the stable indicator - hunt for structure, not content.

steps.title: Block, isolate, and tune
steps.caption: The team blocks the C2 addresses, isolates the host, and tunes the variance rule to zero false positives per week.
steps.defender: keep the analytics rule after cleanup - padding will return in the next campaign.
